documents.unit: Office of the General Counsel (Academic Misconduct Policy 4.1.7)
documents.title: Academic Misconduct Policy
documents.summary: A general academic misconduct policy that lists 'unauthorized use of artificial intelligence' as one form of cheating. It gives no guidance on permitted uses, disclosure, or who grants authorization; the rest covers misconduct procedures and appeals.
documents.stance_why: Coder A said delegates, coder B restrict. The only AI text is the bullet 'unauthorized use of artificial intelligence' under Cheating; the policy never says who authorizes AI or what is authorized, and the neighbouring bullet ties approval to the instructor ('specifically approved by the instructor'). It sets no default rule and no list of permitted uses, so it sets no AI stance itself and defers to those who authorize, which is delegates rather than restrict.

units.why: The bullet lists 'unauthorized use of artificial intelligence' among prohibited conduct under Cheating, so it classifies unauthorized AI use as misconduct (P36). It binds students, and its operative effect is on misconduct, so the phase is when-misuse. It is not P06 because it states no fallback for silent syllabi, and not P04 because it does not say who decides.
units.policy: Unauthorized use of artificial intelligence is cheating, a form of academic misconduct for which students are subject to disciplinary action.
units.resolution_why: Both coders found this unit with identical anchor, actor, phase, modality, policy_type and unit_stance. Wording differed slightly; the source says prohibited conduct 'for which students are subject to disciplinary action' and lists the bullet under Cheating, so A's wording is kept as faithful.

notes: Single thin AI mention. Non-AI provisions (appeals, syllabus pointer to the misconduct policy) not coded.
